Subject: Hardware commitment vs retainer options for Soteria on-prem deployment

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the demo last week — the on-prem build looks promising. Before we loop procurement, I wanted to surface two commercial paths Soteria is weighing so we can get illustrative numbers and mechanics:

1) Hardware commitment (CAPEX-heavy): Soteria either purchases the GPU servers outright or signs a 36-month node commitment with Redwood. In that scenario we want the platform fee amortized against the commitment and a smaller monthly SRE retainer. Important to our CFO: exit protections (what happens if we downsize year 2) and license escrow options.

2) Retainer / op-ex model: Minimal upfront hardware commitment, monthly platform fee, and a larger SRE retainer to cover onboarding + run. Preferable if we want to avoid hardware procurement cycles, but it increases OPEX.

We also like a hybrid pilot-to-prod path where an initial 6-month pilot is on reserved nodes with implementation credits that can be applied to a later hardware commit.

Can you send: 
- A short matrix comparing unit economics (36m amortized vs 12m retainer) including sample invoice phasing
- Typical support tiers and what’s covered in the SRE retainer vs per-incident support
- Your proposals on exit protection and escrow language (high level)

Attaching our technical requirements doc so you can map SKU sizing. Looking for a short call to review numbers — are you free Wednesday afternoon PT?

Thanks,
Alyssa Monroe
Sr. Procurement Manager | Soteria Tech

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the clear outline and for the sizing doc. Good week to align on this. I pulled together three pragmatic commercial options (high level) and an illustrative invoice phasing spreadsheet — attached.

Option 1 — Hardware-commitment (36-month):
- Customer commits to N dedicated nodes (or purchases equivalent hardware).
- Platform fee: typically amortized over 36 months; we can offer a 12–15% discount vs list if committed and prepaid year 1.
- SRE retainer: reduced (baseline on-call + 40 hrs/month) — lower monthly OPEX.
- Exit protection: 12-month notice with limited downgrade credits (pro-rated over remaining term). Escrow options available on request.

Option 2 — Retainer / OpEx (monthly):
- No hardware commitment, platform fee billed monthly.
- SRE retainer: higher (baseline + implementation hours included for first 90 days).
- Better for teams avoiding CAPEX but ~20–30% higher TCO over 36 months vs Option 1.

Option 3 — Pilot-to-commit (hybrid):
- 6-month pilot on reserved capacity; implementation credit applied toward hardware commit within 6 months of pilot end.
- We typically offer a pilot credit equal to 25% of pilot fees if customer converts to a 36-month commit.

Request: can you confirm which commercial levers are highest priority for Soteria (lower up-front, lowest long-term TCO, or operational flexibility)? That will let us tailor numbers.

Next steps: I propose a 45-minute working session Wednesday 2026-06-23 2:00pm PT to run a short model and show invoice phasing options. Marissa from our commercial ops will join to walk the invoice templates.

Attaching: RI_onprem_pricing_scenarios.xlsx (illustrative invoices, sample amortization rows).

Best,
Priyom Das

Thanks Priyom — quick legal/ops thoughts for the working session. Sending high-level positions so Alyssa and procurement have visibility before Wednesday. Attached is a redline of our standard T&Cs.

Our baseline negotiating positions:
- Exit protection: we can offer a 12-month notice period with pro-rated credits on pre-paid platform fees. For hardware-commits where customer owns the servers, we permit early termination but require reimbursement of remaining amortized platform fee unless customer transfers commitment to another Redwood customer.
- Escrow / IP: we can offer a limited licenseed escrow for model artifacts necessary to run the inference stack; full source escrow is exceptional and requires senior sign-off.
- Implementation credits: suggest 10% implementation credit for a 36-month hardware commitment (applied against year-1 platform fee) — this is below our upper range but preserves runway for SRE engagement.
- Prepayment discounts: standard is 10% for annual prepay; 15% if customer prepays 24+ months. We should consider a 12% anchor for Soteria if they commit to a 36m term and prepay year 1.
- SLA carveouts: support tiers clearly state time-to-respond and covered vs out-of-scope activities (we need to list third-party HW maintenance as customer responsibility unless a managed HW add-on is purchased).

For the working session we should bring: a) amortization table (Priyom), b) SRE retainer scope doc (Marissa), c) redline T&Cs (attached). I recommend we be prepared to table a hybrid concession: 12% prepay discount + 10% implementation credit if they convert pilot to commit within 6 months.

Attaching: Redwood_T&Cs_redlines.docx

—Irene

Priyom / Irene / Marissa — thanks for the clear options and the redline. After running this past Finance, Soteria prefers the hybrid pilot-to-commit path with the following asks: 

- Pilot: 6 months on reserved nodes with an implementation credit equal to 25% of pilot fees if we sign a 36-month hardware commitment within 90 days of pilot end.
- Conversion terms: 12% prepay discount on year 1 platform fee if we prepay annually; 10% implementation credit applied against that prepay.
- Exit protection: we accept a 12-month notice with pro-rated credits and would like explicit language allowing for a one-time downgrade of up to 25% of committed nodes in year 2 without penalty.
- SLA / Onboarding: Request SRE kickoff within 30 days of signature and a fixed 8-week onboarding milestone plan included in the SRE retainer during the pilot.

If that aligns with Redwood’s recommended hybrid concession (Irene’s 12% prepay + 10% implementation credit), we’re ready to proceed to an LOI and sign intent.
